topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Biology
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the module scope and student backgrounds, and introduces the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer as a Disease of Genetic Change and Differentiation Failure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an accumulation of genetic alterations leading to the breakdown of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, and discuss methods for studying tumor cells.

topics.label: Benign versus Malignant Tumors: Invasion, Progression, and Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish benign from malignant neoplasms by examining invasive and metastatic behavior, stepwise histological progression, and tumor naming conventions.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer explains the physiological and mechanical processes by which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death in patients.

topics.label: Comparative Cancer Incidence Across Tissues and Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and mortality rates of various tumor types in humans and compare cancer susceptibility across different animal species.

topics.label: Principles and Practice of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors present clinically and assess the efficacy, histology, and practical challenges of screening programs for various cancers.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by reiterating the learning outcomes and looking forward to upcoming practical sessions.
